summary: Run it alone, without a companion. It changes one row (unpooler decode_16), and the profile's kernel time (_bf16_swapab_kernel vs nvjet's 17.6 us) shows directly whether it worked, but the case for a gain is weak: the BLOCK_T 32 version of this kernel took 18.4 us on this row and 18.1 us at m=32, so a flat or slightly slower row is the likeliest result.
justification: Mechanism: at m=16 the full-width unpooler is a pure 67.1 MB weight stream (floor 14.1 us). nvjet reaches 17.6 us, about 3.8 TB/s. The proposed kernel uses master's constants: grid (128,1), SPLIT_K 1, BLOCK_W 64, BLOCK_K 256, 4 stages. That is 40 KB per stage with BLOCK_T 16, so 160 KB of shared memory, still one CTA per SM on 128 of 132 SMs, each CTA streaming 512 KB over 16 K-steps. That is the same occupancy and the same bytes in flight as the BLOCK_T 32 variant. BLOCK_T 16 shrinks the x tile and the wgmma N size, but neither one is the bottleneck for a DRAM-bound stream. The evidence agrees. Prior run unpooler-full-m16-swapab-route (05782267) with BLOCK_T 32: kernel 18.4 us on this row. The same kernel at m=32 on master: 18.1 us. Pooler with BLOCK_T 16 at m=16 (same 67 MB, split-K 2): 19.2 us. All of these are at or above nvjet's 17.6. Weakest link: the 'faster' prediction rests on two things that do not carry over. (1) The 1.022x paired reading in 05782267 is noise. Its SGLang baseline_ns was 18.9 us, against 18.4 in the master run, while the kernel itself was 0.8 us slower than nvjet, and the row was judged flat (1.0129). (2) The qkv 18% and o 10-19% gains came from replacing mma.sync kernels that put the tokens on M with wgmma, not from going from BLOCK_T 32 to 16. My prediction for the kernel: about 17.9-18.4 us against nvjet's 17.6, so the row is flat to slightly slower. The best case is about +2% on one row out of 30, roughly +0.07% on the headline, well inside the ±1.5% noise. The expected shapes and directions do match the gating: only cfg n == 8192 with 9 <= m <= 16 changes, and the only scored row with that shape is unpooler decode_16. Not a duplicate: the do-not-retry list is empty, and the 'do not retry in this form' note on 05782267 covers BLOCK_T 32 on the older 8b9ad43 base.
confounders: bf16-restack-m16-swapab-router-swapab-m32: it landed the SWAPAB16 path and the BLOCK_T 16 compile of _bf16_swapab_kernel that this change reuses. It shares the kernel, not timing or memory traffic. There is no interaction, other than that a compile-variant problem in it would show up here too.

bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton: SWAPAB_CFG['unpooler'] (8192,4096,1,256,4) is copied as a constant into a separate SWAPAB16_CFG key. Retuning that entry later would not change this key. m=17..32 is not touched, so there is no shared-path confound.

restack-three-cell-wins-router-unpooler-cluster-m8-nn-m128: the ouns branch runs first in kernel_fn, but it takes only n == 1024, and the NN-layout path takes only m=65..128. Neither matches cfg n=8192 at m=16, so neither can interact. The one adjacent risk is _swapab16_key: if it is written so that an n==1024 m<=8 call no longer returns 'unpooler_slice', the slice fallback after the ouns gate changes. Check the attempt diff for exactly this.
sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: it provides the nvjet incumbent that is being replaced. That incumbent's 17.6 us is the bar, and nothing about it varies between runs.
interference: No companion is needed. The change swaps exactly one kernel on one scored row. The run's profile gives that row's top kernel and its time, so _bf16_swapab_kernel's time against nvjet's 17.6 us (and against BLOCK_T 32's 18.4 us) answers the hypothesis directly, whatever the headline does. Reverting a landed hypothesis (ab-revert) would only take away the infrastructure this change depends on, and an ab-tune of the stage count or BLOCK_K would be a new hypothesis, not a disambiguator. Both would cost a scored run each, and neither would make a gain or a loss easier to read than the kernel time already does. The headline and the 29 other rows will drift by ±1.5% as before (05782267 was labelled 'regression' purely from untouched rows), so the harvest should judge this run on that row's kernel time, not on the headline.
rules_flags: No rule problem in the change itself. Dispatch depends on cfg and shapes only, and SPLIT_K 1 means no workspace or tickets, no host sync and no state derived from the inputs.

Correctness coverage: no correctness test exercises the full-width unpooler at m=9..16 (tests are m 5, 130 and 1000). The only check on this path is the scored decode_16 row itself. The prepare-time fp32 self-check (rel L2 > 1e-2 -> drop the key) is in the Risk section but not in the change paragraph, so the builder may leave it out. Add it, on synthetic random x, never on inputs from data, and make sure the threshold is no looser than checks.py's bound for bf16 layers.
Make sure the warm-up covers m = 9..16 (not just m_top), so the timed call never JIT-compiles. M is do_not_specialize, so a single compile should cover them all, but warm each m as the change says.
open_questions: Run on a scored submit: is one row with a likely 0-2% kernel delta worth a scored run, when the best case moves the headline by about 0.07%? The deciding question is whether a flat or slower result closes the unpooler-full m<=16 swap-AB line (I think it should), not whether it can be read.

If the kernel comes in at 18.0 us or more, should the harvest record 'swap-AB Triton cannot beat nvjet on the full-width 67 MB unpooler at m<=32 with one CTA per SM' as a do-not-retry, so that further BLOCK_T or stage variants are not tried? The next lever would be bytes in flight per SM (two CTAs per SM, or a TMA bulk stream), not the tile shape.

Pooler with BLOCK_T 16 (19.2 us) is slower than the unpooler with BLOCK_T 32 (18.1 us) on the same 67 MB. Is that because of the pooler's split-K 2 reduction, or its shorter rows (k=8192 vs n=8192)? The answer would sharpen the prediction for this run.
